name: Japan
tagline: Tokyo to Kyoto, with a three- and five-year-old in tow.
intro: Thirteen days of temples, theme parks, ramen and ninja trials — planned around little legs, early nights and the very real art of getting tickets in Japan. Everything we booked, when we booked it, and how you can do it too.

essentials.title: Stay connected
essentials.body: An eSIM is the easiest way to have maps and translation from the moment you land. Install it before you fly and switch it on at Narita.

essentials.title: IC card (Suica / PASMO / ICOCA)
essentials.body: Tap-and-go for trains, buses, konbini and vending machines. Add a Suica to Apple Wallet before you leave, or buy a physical card at the airport. Children 6+ pay child fares — under-6s ride free with an adult.

essentials.title: JR Pass vs single tickets
essentials.body: After the 2023 price rise, a simple Tokyo–Kyoto return is usually cheaper on single Shinkansen tickets booked through smartEX than a 7-day JR Pass. Run your own route through a fare calculator before buying.

essentials.title: Travelling with little ones
essentials.body: A compact, fold-in-one-hand stroller is essential — stations have lifts but they can be a walk away. Most department stores have superb baby rooms. Konbini onigiri and bananas saved us more than once.

essentials.title: Luggage forwarding (takkyubin)
essentials.body: Send big suitcases hotel-to-hotel between Tokyo and Kyoto and ride the Shinkansen with just a day bag. Book at your hotel front desk the day before.
